title: [$175] Avoid repeating full search and filtering work while typing in SearchRouter
body:
## Background The Search Router is the suggestion window you open with Cmd+K / Ctrl+K or the search icon in the header. As you type, the UI filters and renders local suggestions right away. Backend search results arrive later and fill the remaining slots, up to the 20-result limit. ## Problem To build local suggestions, the app processes the full report collection and builds contact options on every debounced keystroke. On accounts with thousands of reports and large contact lists, this brute-force filtering blocks the main thread. Under 4x CPU slowdown: - Median latency before the first suggestions commit: **307–329 ms** - React render time per query: **over 310 ms** - UI frame freezes: **up to 576 ms** Current Sentry telemetry covers only opening the router and the first list render. Keystroke work is not measured. ## Solution 1. **Telemetry baseline:** Add sampled Sentry measurements for debounced queries. Track query execution and list render durations across platforms and account sizes. Do not record query text. 2. **Search option index:** Add an in-memory search index so query matching and ranking no longer depend on building every UI option. - Store the index as a `Map` keyed by `reportID` or `accountID`. Each row holds: - **Search text:** a pre-normalized, lowercased string with titles, subtitles, logins/emails, and participant names. - **Sort key:** the report timestamp / last read time (or contact display name), used for ranking. - Build rows in the background during idle time, and update them incrementally as Onyx data changes. - On each keystroke, iterate `Map.values()` with a `String.includes()` check. Stream matches through the existing bounded `MaxHeap` (`optionsOrderBy`) to get the top candidate IDs. - Format and validate only those candidates with `getSearchOptions`. It stays the single source of truth for formatting, permissions, and query-dependent filtering (`excludeLogins`, `includeCurrentUser`). 3. **Rollout:** Use the Sentry telemetry to confirm responsiveness gains and monitor memory use. **Code clarity is a requirement.** Keep the index cleanly isolated, and document its data structures and lookup flow so contributors can understand it and avoid misusing it. ## Expected impact (from PoC benchmarks) - Time to first result commit drops about 75% (~320 ms → ~70 ms under 4x CPU slowdown). - React render duration drops about 75% (~320 ms → ~80 ms). Peak frame freezes drop about 27% on Web and 51% on iOS. - Incremental Onyx updates cost about 3 ms per change. ## Trade-offs - **Memory:** Retained JS heap grows by ~89 MB (+21.6% warm) to ~171 MB (+41.7% cold) on a large test account, because of cached search rows. - **Startup work:** Pre-warming uses ~144 ms of total CPU time in idle windows, spread over ~3.9 s after startup. ## Benchmark setup (Web) - Automated Playwright benchmark, Chromium headed at 1440x900, development web build. - Large test account: 2,406 reports, 11,840 personal details, 194 policies. Network API traffic blocked to isolate client-side work. - 4x CPU throttling plus Onyx churn (background writes every 200 ms across 20 reports). - 10 measured runs per version, plus 1 discarded warm-up run. PoC: https://github.com/software-mansion-labs/expensify-app-fork/pull/420 _Reported in [Slack](https://expensify.slack.com/archives/C08CZDJFJ77/p1791270686643419)._
